title: Autonomic region rebalancer: standby priming probes and fallback model inventory
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We need an autonomous orchestration layer to decide when and how to bring warm standby regions online and which fallback model variants to route to during capacity or regional outages. Current warm standby behavior is manual and relies on coarse health signals which results in prolonged failover times and cold-cache penalties. Goal: Implement a readiness-check state machine plus a model-variant inventory & compatibility model so the router can: 1) validate warm standby readiness with deterministic probes, 2) prime local KV caches and model I/O without exposing production traffic, 3) select fallback model variants by quality/cost/latency heuristics, and 4) integrate with autoscaler and routing policies for seamless activation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Readiness-check state machine implemented in router orchestration that transitions through: UNKNOWN -> PROBING -> PRIMED -> READY -> ACTIVE. 2) At least three distinct probe types implemented (synthetic inference, prefix-KV probe, and kernel-compatibility probe) and passing criteria configurable per region/tier. 3) Warm priming executes under a traffic-isolated mode (no customer-origin traffic consumption) and achieves >=70% KV cache hit rate for typical 256-token sessions within priming window. 4) Router leverages model-variant inventory to select compatible fallback with documented quality delta and cost multiplier. 5) Failover time from detectable region outage to traffic ramp to ACTIVE < 60s in controlled test. 6) End-to-end automated tests + chaos test demonstrating graceful rollback to previous region on mis-priming.
design_notes: High-level approach: 1) Introduce a ReadinessProbeManager that runs configurable probe suites per candidate standby. Probes are lightweight, idempotent, and tagged by probe-class. 2) Define probe classes: SYNTH_RESPONSE (synthetic prompts to measure latency/quality), KV_PRIME (prefix writes/reads to populate KV cache), KERNEL_CHECK (probe of selected kernels and quantization paths to ensure binary compatibility), and MODEL_LOAD (verify model weights loaded and memory pressure within threshold). 3) Add a priming mode in runtime that accepts 'priming-token' header to route internal priming traffic without affecting telemetry billing. 4) Build a fallback-model-inventory: a catalog per model family mapping compatible variants, expected relative latency, and calibrated quality deltas. 5) Readiness state machine exposes metrics and traces for each transition; transition thresholds derived from historical region SLAs and synthetic benchmarks. 6) Autoscaler hooks: if priming extends > priming_timeout, autoscaler can opportunistically scale underlying pool. 7) Safety: require at least two passing probe classes to reach PRIMED; require human approval if primed time exceeds max_priming_duration for enterprise-tier customers.
probe_spec_examples: - SYNTH_RESPONSE: 5 warm synthetic prompts per minute, 95th-percentile latency < regional_slo_ms*1.5, generation quality >= baseline BLEU-like metric threshold. - KV_PRIME: write 100 prefix tokens representative of top-100 prompts, verify reads return tokens and achieve KV-hit >= 70%. - KERNEL_CHECK: run a micro-benchmark for attention kernel on target hardware for 20ms sample; validate no fallback to slow execution path. - MODEL_LOAD: request load endpoint and confirm GPU memory usage delta within expected band and model state READY.
state_machine: UNKNOWN -> PROBING -> PRIMED -> READY -> ACTIVE. Transitions: UNKNOWN->PROBING triggered by policy (region priority, capacity alarms). PROBING->PRIMED when >=2 probe classes pass within timewindow. PRIMED->READY after KV_PRIME hit-rate and SYNTH_RESPONSE stability for primed_stability_window. READY->ACTIVE after canary traffic ramp validation and latency tail checks. Active->UNKNOWN on fail signal or explicit drain.
routing_policy_changes: - Integrate with existing smart routing policy to consult readiness state before routing production traffic. - Tier routing: prefer same-tier regions; if standby READY in higher tier, policy can favor higher-tier READY standby with cost-aware multiplier. - Fallback selection: pick fallback with minimal expected quality delta within latency constraint. - Provide per-customer override: enforce 'no-autoswitch' flag for enterprise customers during scheduled maintenance.
observability_and_metrics: Expose metrics per-region: readiness_state, probe_pass_count, kv_hit_rate, synth_latency_p50/p95/p99, kernel_latency, priming_duration_seconds. Emit events to Console: readiness.transition, priming.started, priming.completed, fallback.selected. Add traces for probe runs and decision-making. Add alerting rule: priming_duration > 10m or failed_probe_rate > 30% triggers PagerDuty routing to SRE.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for state machine transitions and probe aggregation logic. 2) Integration test harness in staging that simulates region outage and validates failover < 60s with primed standby. 3) Load test with representative token distribution, measuring KV-hit improvement post-priming. 4) Chaos experiment: flip model-variant compatibility to induce KERNEL_CHECK failures and assert rollback and safe fallback to alternate variant. 5) Postmortem drills with on-call team to exercise runbook.
implementation_tasks: Implement KV_PRIME probe and priming traffic tag
Extend model catalog with variant compatibility metadata
